look_here_first: Compare the whole plant against Texas pricklypear before counting spines. O. macrorhiza is usually a low, sprawling grassland cactus with smaller pads close to the ground. Then check the areoles: relatively few permanent spines, often with the main spine strongly bent or deflexed near its base, plus orange-brown glochids.

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: low sprawling or radiating succulent shrub, often close to the ground

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: flattened photosynthetic cladodes/pads commonly smaller than the large Texas-pricklypear anchor

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: true cactus areoles repeated over the pads

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: areoles with brown wool and dense orange to brown glochids

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: permanent spines commonly few; main spine often strongly bent at the base and deflexed

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: large showy flowers yellow with reddish or rose-red pigmentation toward the petal bases in the detailed Williamson treatment

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: inferior ovary with areoles on the surrounding pericarpel tissue

key_traits.label: Habit
key_traits.text: Often forms a low radial plant with branches/pads touching the ground rather than a taller shrubby pricklypear.

key_traits.label: Areole
key_traits.text: Areoles are the family-defining structure; in this species the wool/glochids and few bent permanent spines are useful comparison characters.

key_traits.label: Spines
key_traits.text: The strongest permanent spine is often bent sharply near its base and angles downward. Do not use spine count alone.

key_traits.label: Flower
key_traits.text: Large radial flowers with many free perianth segments and numerous stamens; local treatment describes yellow inner segments with rose-red color toward the base.

lookalikes.differences: Against O. engelmannii var. lindheimeri, use overall low habit, smaller pad proportions, areole spacing, glochid color, and the bent/deflexed main spine as a character suite—not a single feature.
